i'm fine with a founder selling enough shares to pay off their mortgage.

i want ambition. financial anxiety isn't a requirement.

paying for ai shouldn't mean buying its agreement.

if my plan is bad, i want the product to push back on me.

ai founders: build for someone doing the job for the first time.

making an expert faster is useful. letting a beginner take on work they couldn't even attempt before is the more interesting ambition.

for @anthropicai, i’d start with two numbers: future compute spend already locked in, and future revenue already locked in. how far apart are they?

that matters more to me than the growth rate alone.

cheaper homework help is too small a goal for ai education.

build a whole curriculum around the thing a kid won't stop asking about.

startup founders: let your best engineers get rich doing engineering.

a bigger paycheck shouldn't require becoming a manager.
founders: i'd rather you walk away from a huge prospect than reshape the whole startup into their internal tools team.

ai coding tools need a “try to break it” button as prominent as “build.”

i want a ruthless tester, not just an eager builder.

i want ai that negotiates my bills down, not ai that gets better at selling me things.

build for the buyer's wallet, not the advertiser's.

getting an allocation isn't the same as getting a good deal.

if the pitch is mostly about who else is in, i want to spend a lot more time on the price.

mineral startups: show me the customer willing to sign a long-term purchase agreement.

that interests me more than another deck explaining why the material is strategically important.

i'd pay more for ai software that needs fewer people to operate it.

charge me per seat and you make less when you deliver exactly what i want.

my bar for reindustrialization is material shipped, not deposits announced.

china was the world's top producer of 39 mineral commodities in 2023, per USGS.
i wouldn't call ten ai startups diversified if every investment case depends on the same company buying them.

software founders: let customers export everything.

if your retention plan depends on making departure painful, i don't buy the product thesis.

ai founders: if a better model makes the feature you're proudest of unnecessary, delete the fucking feature.

that makes me more interested in the company, not less.

i'd rather see france simplify permits for power projects than host a glamorous ai summit.

make it easier to build the fucking power supply.

i want codex on iphone to ask for a decision, not turn my phone into a tiny fucking IDE.

show me what's blocking the work and enough context to choose. then let me put the phone away.

my test for french industrial policy:

can a startup win a government contract while it still can't afford a government relations team?

i like businesses that can pay their owners without needing a richer buyer to show up.

dividends aren't a boomer aesthetic. cash coming back is part of the fucking point of ownership.
consumer ai: “save an hour” is fine. “start the business you couldn’t afford to staff” is the pitch i give a shit about.

vcs: a founder should be able to tell you your advice is wrong without wondering whether that kills the next check.

you're buying equity, not agreement.

ai tutors should help curious kids outrun the syllabus, not keep pace with the classroom.

if a kid wants to learn calculus early, fucking go. help them get there.

investment committees should have to write down what would turn a pass into a check.

if it's “a famous fund leads the next round,” spare everyone the diligence theater.

vcs: if a company could be a great investment but is “too small for our fund,” maybe your fund is too fucking big.

i'd reconsider the fund size before reconsidering what counts as a good business.

where do i want my ai to be a cheapskate?

sorting my inbox? absolutely.
reviewing my contract? fuck no.

i want the spending to follow the cost of a mistake.

i'd rather have an ai agent with a great undo button than one marketed as flawless.

give me a fucking reverse gear.

personal ai should let me fire the vendor and keep the memory.

years of context should compound for me, not become the reason i’m stuck paying you. making me start over is a shitty retention strategy.

founders: don't negotiate your valuation for the college group chat.

i'd rather have a round i can build on than a number that makes me look rich.

being the least liquid founder at dinner is a shitty reason to sell your company.

take a deal you actually want. your friends cashing out doesn't mean you're late.

jailbreaking chatgpt doesn't declassify shit.

getting it to repeat your conspiracy is not evidence for it. show me a source outside the chat window.

consumer ai should negotiate for me, not sell businesses access to me.

if i’m giving an agent my whole life as context, use it to get me a better deal. not to make me an easier fucking sale.

startups: a big contract should buy your product, not veto power over your roadmap.

don’t sign up to be someone’s underpaid internal software team.
my ideal ai will argue with the assignment. if the project is dumb, tell me before handing me a beautiful plan to execute it.

if all ten of your ai investments need the same incumbent to fuck up, that's one bet—not ten.

i'd diversify the ways i can be right, not just the cap tables.

vcs: i'm fine with a founder taking enough secondary to get rent off their mind.

i want them thinking clearly for the next decade. i don't need financial anxiety as proof they're all in.

ai tutors should compete on how fast the kid can solve the problem without them.

not how long they can keep the kid chatting. don't build another fucking engagement loop and call it education.
ai products should eat their own retry costs. i want to pay for finished work, not every attempt your agent needs to get there.

vcs: raising a bigger fund is not a reason to tell a founder to swing bigger.

make the case on the business, not your fucking fund math.

ai investing: i want founders hoping spud is ridiculously good.

if your business needs the next model to disappoint, i don't want to own it.

ten approvers. ten copilots. still ten approvals.

i’d start by asking which handoffs ai lets us delete, not how to speed up both sides of every handoff.

the ai market i’m most excited about: work that never got commissioned because expertise was too expensive.

“i can finally afford an expert” is a hell of a lot more ambitious than “who can i fire?”

custom software should be disposable.

one deal. one launch. one weird problem. build the tool, use it, delete it.

making every ai-built tool earn a permanent place in the stack is a stupid constraint.

if the price already assumes an ai startup wins, what’s left for me when it does?

i can love the size of the market and still hate the entry price.

meta says muse wonder took over a year of research and infrastructure work.

good. i don't want frontier research run like a fucking quarterly content calendar. give the team room to be ambitious.

ai founders: i’d hire the customer who hacked together a janky fix over the candidate with the polished ai thesis.

i want someone pissed off enough to do something about the problem.

meta’s calling muse wonder frontier. cool.

give me the job you’d trust it to do that you still won’t hand another model. that’s the part of the launch i give a damn about.

ai founders: let customers bring their own agents.

if your product only works when your chatbot owns the whole damn conversation, i'd question how much product is actually there.

ai founders: giving an agent my credit card shouldn't mean unlimited permission to spend.

i want to assign the work and the budget together. build spending permissions into the damn product.

founders: let your best engineer kill a product requirement, not just ship it faster.

paying for judgment and then making the spec untouchable is fucking wasteful.

founder secondary can be good for the cap table.

if getting rich makes it easier for the founder to turn down an acquisition and build something bigger, i’m for it. i care whether liquidity buys more ambition, not whether cashing out violates your religion.

founders: don't hire a chief of staff because you hate saying no.

make the damn decision before you turn your reluctance into someone else's job.

if a customer wants to invest in your startup, cool. i'd still ask for a bigger contract.

i want to see that conviction in the purchasing budget too.

vc: wanting more ownership is your problem, not a reason for a founder to raise more fucking money.

adjust your check size. don’t ask them to adjust their burn.

a follow-on check should beat the new deals you could fund with the same money.

“we’re already in” is not a fucking investment thesis.

my bar for medical ai: an abnormal breast scan should set a coordinated next step in motion.

the patient should not have to become the damn project manager.

quantum founders: if you can’t build the company without that scientist, give them a ridiculous amount of equity.

i wouldn’t risk losing them just to keep the cap table looking normal.

why make pc builders the target for cloud gaming? let them enjoy building pcs.

geforce now says gears of war: e-day launches this week. i’d go after people who want to play without making hardware a hobby. that’s where i’d focus the business.

ai founders: getting someone to a breast screening appointment is worth building a company around.

make the scheduling and paperwork disappear. you don’t need to invent a new diagnostic to build an important healthcare company.

if starlink buys low-band spectrum, does it need to own the customer too?

i’d rather make carriers compete to distribute it than build a whole damn sales operation just for starlink to send the bill.

if starlink buys low-band spectrum, my bar is simple: make the phone i already own work in more places.

not another damn gadget to charge.

hardware founders: bring a simulation we can mess with, not just a beautiful render.

change an assumption. try a different design. i’d rather spend the meeting doing that than debating the damn deck.

i want software that makes it cheap to try shit and be wrong.

i’d take a great undo button over another tutorial telling me to be careful.

software founders: how much of your roadmap would you still want to build if your biggest customer left?

i’d worry if the answer is almost none.

my ideal enterprise software demo: give the customer the keyboard and shut the fuck up.

no coaching. no grabbing it back if they get stuck. i want to see what you're actually selling.

ai tutor founders: a kid no longer needing your help should be the goal, not a retention problem.

celebrate the graduation. let the streak end.

i want to see an apartment building designed around robots from day one, not just a robot expected to handle whatever weird shit we’ve built.

change the building too.

my favorite ambition for home robotics is helping your parents stay in their own house.

not a smart speaker with a cuter face. a machine built to do the physical shit they can’t safely do anymore.

energy founders: a date you can actually deliver power is a hell of a product.

i’d put that ahead of the speech about why your technology deserves to win.

my energy abundance test: does a new factory look like a huge customer or a fucking inconvenience?

i want the energy business excited when someone wants to build more.

show me where the ai agent sits on the org chart before showing me its cute avatar.

what does it own? which calls can it make? who answers when it fucks up?

i don’t want an ai game that’s just a knight with a chat window.

i want to try some stupid shit the designer never considered and have the game respond.

“at least i can get into this one” is a shit investment thesis.

i’d pass on the weaker version of a hot company, even if the better one won’t let me in.

telecom ai founders: “we use open models” isn’t the pitch.

in @nvidia’s telecom survey, 89% of respondents say open source models and software are important to their company’s ai strategy.

tell me which line item in the operator’s budget you’re coming for.

i want coding agents in the hands of the warehouse manager who knows exactly why the software sucks.

not so they can quit and start a saas company. so they can fix the damn thing and keep running the warehouse.

i want to switch ai products without doing the whole “here’s my life story” thing again.

my context should come with me. keep me because you do more with it, not because leaving is a pain in the ass.

i want an ai buyer that’s willing to tell the seller to fuck off.

if it gets paid when i buy, i don’t want it deciding whether i need the thing. i want it representing me.

if the team doing the work barely owns the upside, i’d fix the cap table before celebrating the next round.

a company can be fundable and still have fucked-up incentives.

an ai product should be allowed to finish.

if it solves my problem and i close the tab, that’s a win. don’t make the agent invent more shit for me to do just to keep me around.

an ai tutor for ambitious adults who want to be beginners in private is worth building.

no audience. no embarrassment. no pretending you got it.

ask the same dumb question until it clicks.

i’d make coding agents maintain what they build as part of training.

cool, you shipped it. now add the next feature without ripping apart everything you just built.

wanting the best intelligence to be ownable is a big fucking ambition.

i want serious capital behind open-weight ai. being open shouldn’t mean aiming lower.

free compute is a trial, not proof of product-market fit.

i want to see who’s still there when the credits run out.

i’d give startups a compute budget they’re allowed to waste.

if every experiment needs a business case first, that’s procurement with an r&d label.

i’d rather a vc say “too small for our fund” than “not worth building.”

if the problem is your fund size, don’t make it sound like the founder has a bad business.

if your new operator needs permission to change anything the last one built, you hired a caretaker.

give them something they can actually rip up and rebuild.

before paying a recruiter to find your next operator, ask who everyone calls when shit breaks.

i’d interview that person first. being on your payroll shouldn’t count against them.

a founder taking ops back after an exec leaves can be a good reset.

i’d put a date on handing it off again, though. “i’ll cover it for now” is an easy way to give yourself a second full-time job.

pro rata is a right, not an auto-renewal.

i’d still want a reason to buy at the new price. “we already own it” isn’t a buy case.

i’d give agents much bigger jobs if i could undo the whole thing when they screw up.

that’s higher on my list than another demo.

if your ai startup pitch is how few employees you need, you’re answering the wrong question for me.

what can you build now that wasn’t worth attempting before?

i’m fine with a founder taking some money off the table.

i want them hungry to build, not desperate to sell the company just to get access to their own net worth.

if Nike drops on earnings, i want the buy case without “it used to trade at a higher multiple.”

remembering the old multiple isn’t valuing the business.

why make matching China in every mineral the goal?

USGS ranked China first globally in production of 39 mineral commodities in 2023.

i’d put the money behind the dependencies we can least afford. finish those projects rather than try to cover the whole list.

GeForce NOW says CONTROL Resonant is available at launch. tell me what i can play, not what i need to buy.
pick the vintage receiver if you like how it sounds. it doesn’t also have to beat a modern stereo on fidelity.

let the software do its job. i don’t want another app to manage.
